history.dynasty: Legendary Treta Yuga origin; archaeological remains from the Vishnukundin period (4th-5th century CE); excavated Gupta-style shrines dated to the 5th century CE; renovated in modern times
history.period: Legend: Treta Yuga; archaeology: 4th-5th century CE onwards
history.summary: Keesaragutta Temple (Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy) stands on a hillock at Keesara, about 30 km from Hyderabad. Legend says Rama installed the Swayambhu Siva lingam here to atone for killing Ravana: Hanuman was sent to Varanasi for a lingam but returned late, so Shiva himself presented a lingam to Rama - hence 'Swayambhu Linga', called Ramalingeswara because Rama installed it. Hanuman returned with 101 lingams and scattered them around the hill when his own was not installed; they are still found and worshipped across the area. To pacify Hanuman, Rama ordained that he be worshipped first and named the hill Kesarigiri (Hanuman, son of Kesari), colloquially transformed to Keesara/Keesaragutta. The ancient village Keesara was known as Gatika, a famed educational institution in the 3rd century AD. Excavations exposed Vishnukundin-period fort walls, 5th-century Gupta-style shrine ruins, and a 5th-century Telugu label inscription read 'Thalachuvanru'/'Thulachuvanru' - the earliest known Telugu inscription in Telangana state. Excavated artefacts are displayed at the Centenary Heritage Museum, Hyderabad. CSV CORRECTION: the CSV lists town 'Hyderabad', but the temple is at Keesara, in MEDCHAL-MALKAJGIRI district - town and district recorded as Keesara / Medchal-Malkajgiri (the temple also fell under Rangareddy district in older sources).

name: Keesaragutta Temple
town_description: Keesara (Keesaragutta) is a pilgrimage town on a hillock in Keesara mandal, Medchal-Malkajgiri district, about 30 km northeast of Hyderabad and 12 km from ECIL. The ancient village was known as Gatika, a 3rd-century centre of learning; excavated artefacts are housed at the Centenary Heritage Museum in Hyderabad.
